text:
sara: heads-up — after the jitter distribution tweak rolled at 03:10 we saw a noticeable uptick in tail latency. p50 +1.8%, p95 +6.2% on the hosting fleet.

mike: ugh. is this the change from gaussian -> uniform jitter?

sara: yeah, switched to uniform with a tighter bound to reduce average hold time. the profiler shows microtick alignment resonance: a lot more concurrent microbatches hitting the kernel switch path. KV cache miss rate up ~12% for a few shards.

anil: can you paste the short perf snippet? interested in kernel-switch churn and L2 misses.

sara: here's the trimmed output from the lightweight tracer (only relevant parts):
```
slot_waits: +24%
kernel_switches/sec: +18%
kv_cache_misses/sec: +12%
avg_coalesce_delay: 3.2ms -> 2.1ms
`````

julie: interesting — reducing coalesce delay lowered avg latency for small requests but increased simultaneous batch formation which trips kernel-selection hot path. that could explain p95 regressions.

mike: what were token-budget targets? did those change with the jitter?

sara: no token targets changed. We still cap at 4096 tokens per batch, but effective per-request token alignment changed because microbatches are now lining up more often. bursts are forming slightly larger batches that force kernel-selection in the middle of generation.

anil: two immediate options: revert to previous jitter distribution, or add low-entropy perturbation to break alignment (small randomized per-queue offset).

julie: +1 for per-queue micro-offset. cheaper and we can A/B canary quickly. also consider softening the kernel switch threshold for a small window to avoid mid-token kernel flips (if safe).

mike: can we simulate with production arrival traces? i can run a quick offline replay against the staging runtime with ~24h of traffic to measure resonance.

sara: doing that now. initial staging run shows the same pattern but smaller amplitude. probably need to include exact timestamp distribution and KV hotspot map.

infra-bot: deploy canary triggered by @mike — canary-id=c-20260318-jitter-perturb, capacity=10% across two regions.

mike: running the replay + canary in parallel. hypothesis: add 0.3-0.6ms per-queue micro-offset, keep uniform jitter but widen slightly to avoid synchronization.

anil: also plan: adjust queue policy to favor token-budget-aware coalescing — if a batch is approaching kernel-switch threshold prefer draining a tiny bit earlier instead of waiting for alignment. That should reduce kernel-switch churn at cost of micro increase in avg coalesce delay.

julie: please capture KV miss rate and kernel_switches/sec as primary signals. add a regression alert if p95 increases >4% or kv misses >8% over baseline.

sara: noted. i'll post the replay results and canary metrics in this thread in ~45m. for now rolling the perturbation to canary only. thanks all. :thumbsup:

mike: if perturbation helps we should add a small unit test that checks synthetic pulse arrivals don't align under the jitter distribution — caught us before but worth automating.

sara: good call. i'll add a micro-sim test to eng-runtime repo.```
